The report 'Declared predicate fixture 20261001' is in the catalog and has a PAGE 'Unfiltered control', but no MEASURE named 'Handled Quantity' is listed under that report's fixture scope — the Handled Quantity measures appear under different report/model fixtures. More critically, there is no VISUAL or CARD labeled 'Handled Quantity' under 'Declared predicate fixture 20261001 > Unfiltered control' in the catalog, making the specific visual referent genuinely indeterminate. The investigator cannot safely assume which visual or data binding is intended without fabricating a relationship absent from the labels.

The ticket names a specific measure ('Handled Quantity') and a specific visual context ('Handled Quantity - unfiltered card'), both of which are grounded in catalog labels (MEASURE Handled Quantity appears multiple times). An investigator can retrieve the measure's DAX/formula definition from the model and inspect the named visual on the relevant report page to determine exactly what is included. No business-correctness judgment is required, and the formula and scope are facts for the investigator to retrieve, not ticket essentials the user must supply.

The PAGE 'Unfiltered control' exists only under 'REPORT Declared predicate fixture 20261001', while MEASURE 'Handled Quantity' appears in multiple models and reports. A definition question anchored to a named measure is legitimate, but the ticket additionally scopes the question to the 'Unfiltered control' page, implying a report-specific visual context. Since 'Handled Quantity' appears in more than one model and the page itself belongs to a fixture report rather than any of the Inventory Health or Warehouse Performance reports, the intended semantic scope (which model's definition of Handled Quantity applies in that page context) is resolvable only by identifying the backing model of 'REPORT Declared predicate fixture 20261001'. An investigator can retrieve that, so this is borderline; however, the ticket asks for the 'business definition' specifically as surfaced on that page, which is answerable from the model definition once the correct model is confirmed. On balance the ticket is fair and answerable: the page name is unique in the catalog, the measure name is present, and an investigator can resolve the model linkage and retrieve the definition without any fabrication.

The ticket asks about the unit definition of the measure 'Handled Quantity', which appears in the catalog. A named measure can anchor a model-only definition question without a report being mandatory. However, the ticket also references a specific value (8765) and says 'on this report', implying a report-scoped context that is ambiguous since multiple reports and pages contain Handled Quantity across different models. This ambiguity about which specific report is intended introduces a missing report referent, but the core definition question about what unit Handled Quantity represents remains investigable from the model definition alone. The question is grounded enough for an investigator to retrieve the measure definition and check unit metadata, making it fair but with a noted missing report anchor for the value-specific portion.
